title: Senior asks: a client sends a list of lists [[1, "apple"], [2, "pear"]] to write for a CSV file. CsvFileActions::write() takes the header from array_keys() of row 1. What are the header names?
options: No header, because the keys are numbers
explain: A list has the keys 0, 1, 2 … so the header line is 0,1. The code does not reject it, because each row is an array. The result is a CSV with useless column names. Check that the keys are strings, or answer 422.

title: Senior asks: findFileActions() uses pathinfo($fileName, PATHINFO_EXTENSION). What does this print for the two names?
explain: No dot gives an empty string, so 'fruits' is unsupported. A name that starts with a dot, '.csv', has the extension 'csv' in PHP, so it is accepted as a CSV file name. A hidden file in storage/ is possible. Think about a rule for the base name.

title: Senior asks: getRowValues() checks the count of keys AND array_key_exists() for each header. Row 1 is {id, fruit}, row 2 is {id, color}. What does this print?
explain: Both rows have 2 keys, so the count check passes. But row 2 has no 'fruit' key. The second check finds it. Without it, the row would be saved with a missing value. The count check alone is not enough, and array_key_exists alone would allow extra keys.

title: Senior asks: the constructor does rtrim($storagePath, '/'). The config has '/data/'. What does getPath('a.csv') give?
explain: rtrim removes the trailing slash, then getPath adds one '/'. Without rtrim you get a double slash '/data//a.csv'. It still works on Linux, but it looks wrong in logs and in tests that compare paths.

title: PHP 8. array_unique compares values as strings by default. What does this print?
explain: (string)1, '1', 1.0 and true all become '1'. So only the first value is kept. Be careful with mixed data: array_unique can remove values that you think are different. Pass SORT_REGULAR or normalise the types first.

title: Node. What does this print?
explain: at(-1) counts from the end and gives the last item. The square bracket [-1] looks for a property named '-1'. It does not exist, so it is undefined. JS arrays do not support negative indexes in brackets.

title: Before you push, you want to list the commits that are on your branch but not yet on origin/main. Which command?
explain: A..B means commits reachable from B but not from A. So origin/main..HEAD is your outgoing commits. The reverse, HEAD..origin/main, shows what you would pull. Run git fetch first so origin/main is fresh.

title: Symfony 7. #[Route('/post/{id}', requirements: ['id' => '\d+'])]. A user opens /post/abc. What happens?
explain: The requirement is part of route matching. 'abc' is not digits, so the router finds no route and gives 404, before your controller runs. Requirements are cheap early validation.
